title: למה אי אפשר לדגדג את עצמך — והרובוט שהוכיח למה
summary: Why you can't tickle yourself: the brain's forward model sends a copy of each motor command (cerebellum) and subtracts the predicted touch; Blakemore, Frith & Wolpert's two-robot experiment (1999, 16 adults) — a 200 ms delay or a 90° rotation made self-touch as tickly as external touch; 1998 fMRI (cerebellum, secondary somatosensory cortex); Shergill 2003 tit-for-tat force escalation (0.25 N, +38% per turn, self-made force felt ~half); laughing rats (Berlin 2016), Aristotle and Darwin, Bar-Ilan self-touch research; ms to s, speed × time, and repeated ×1.38 growth.
reviewer_verdict: PASS (2 rounds) — nits left: prose ~1,320 (younger) / ~1,510 (older) words, est. 30–35 min vs the 'כ־25 דקות' tag; kit lint/check missing from the repo so local stand-ins were used; Arto and the AI grader not exercised offline; review copy doesn't declare the sample capability (template); engine strings ('נבדק', '1 יום ברצף') unchanged
